brief: Holds a binary buffer in the engine and reads, cuts, edits and encodes it as Base64, hexadecimal or percent text.
detail: Positions and sizes count bytes from 1, never characters, so a Hebrew letter is 2 bytes and an emoji 4. Reads (Left, Right, Mid, ToHex...) return text and leave the buffer alone; Append, Insert, Remove, Replace, Fill, Resize, Clear and the From... methods change it in place, and their Q forms return the object for chaining. Found today: string/stzBytes.ring is not loaded by stzlib.ring, and it defines a class named stzBytes that clashes with the alias class of stzListOfBytes.ring, so new stzBytes(...) builds the stzListOfBytes alias and none of the methods below exist on it (R14); a negative count, size or length, a Fill value above 255, and a number given to Append stop the Ring process; FromHex empties the buffer on a bad text. The examples were run on an identical copy of the class under another name.
